rl.title: Learn the rules
intro.hist: The national board game of Madagascar, played all over the island. A legend tells of King Ralambo calling his sons home to choose an heir: the elder was absorbed in a difficult Fanorona position, and the younger, Andrianjaka, arrived first and became king.
intro.win: Capture all the opponent's pieces to win (or leave them unable to move). A piece steps along a line; by approaching an enemy piece or withdrawing from one it captures the whole line of enemy pieces beyond.
intro.cult: The game is named by its board: 3×3 "Telo", 5×5 "Dimy", and the most popular 9×5 "Tsivy" played here. In 2007 it was solved by computer: with best play on both sides it is a draw.
tr.board.b: A board of 9×5 points and lines. From a point where diagonals cross (a strong point) a piece can also move diagonally. 22 pieces each fill every point but the centre; White moves first.
tr.move.b: A piece steps along a line to the next empty point, in any direction. A move that captures nothing is called a "paika".
tr.move.task: Move one White piece one step.
tr.move.ok: Good! Pieces move one step along the lines.
tr.must.b: If a capture is possible, you must capture. The glowing pieces are the ones that can capture.
tr.must.task: Find the capture and make it.
tr.must.ok: Right! A capture always comes first.
tr.win.b: Capture all the opponent's pieces to win. Leaving them unable to move also wins.
tr.draw.b: The game is drawn when the same position appears 3 times or 80 moves in a row (both sides) capture nothing. In the endgame, hold the strong points and cut off the enemy's escape routes.
rt.title: Your rating
rt.desc: Opponents (AI from 15 kyu to 5 dan) are chosen to match your rating (starting at 1000). Usually they are close to your level, sometimes stronger or weaker. Win to go up, lose to go down (Elo; the first 10 games move more). Random colour, 5 minutes + 3 seconds per move. No undo, hints or evaluation during the game (you can review afterwards). Running out of time or leaving counts as a loss. AI ratings are this site's own scale.
rt.noEval: No evaluation during a rated game
rt.abandonQ: A rated game is in progress. Leaving now abandons it and counts as a loss. Continue?
ls.title: Lessons
ls.desc: "First steps" for those who just learned the rules, "Tactics" that decide games, and the "Endgame" to finish them. 5 problems per step, 20 points each; 75 to pass. Tactics and endgame problems are checked by the engine, and moves other than the best score by how little they lose.
fb.values: Engine value (1.0 = one piece): your move {a} / best {b}
course.basics.sub: Start here once you know the rules: approach, withdrawal, choosing, capture chains and winning, in practice.
course.tactics.sub: Finding big captures, counting the recaptures, and choosing the right non-capturing move (paika).
course.endgame.sub: Winning with few pieces left: how to hunt down the last ones.
course.graduate: 🎉 "First steps" completed! You are ready to play — try the AI at 15 kyu to 10 kyu.
op.title: Openings (first moves and replies)
op.desc: Fanorona opens with big exchanges right away. Learn White's five first moves and Black's replies to the main ones, along lines this site's engine chose after deep reading. Step through them in "Study", then guess the engine's moves in "Practice".
op.credit: Fanorona was solved in 2007 by M. Schadd et al.: best play leads to a draw (f2-e3A and d3-e3A are shown to draw). The lines and evaluations here were chosen by this site's engine reading a few seconds per position; they are not from the complete solution.

tr.approach.b: If the point just beyond your landing point holds an enemy, it is captured, together with the enemy pieces lined up behind it.
tr.approach.task: Move e2 to e3 and capture the Black line.
tr.approach.ok: Two at once! That was an approach.
tr.withdraw.b: Step straight away from an adjacent enemy and it is captured, together with the enemy pieces lined up behind it.
tr.withdraw.task: Move e3 straight away from the Black piece above it.
tr.withdraw.ng: Move straight away from the Black piece.
tr.choose.b: When one step captures both by approach and by withdrawal, you take only one line. Tap a piece in a dashed ring to choose the line.
tr.choose.task: Move d3 to e3 and take the line of three.
tr.choose.ok: Right! You chose the bigger line.
tr.must.ng: Capture with the piece that can.
tr.chain.b: The capturing piece may capture again in the same turn (or stop). It must change direction each time and may not return to a point it visited.
tr.chain.task: Capture twice or more with the piece on e1.
tr.chain.ok: A capture chain! The count drops fast.
tr.chain.ng: After the first capture, go on and take the next one.
